sources.name: Orbit (The Intelligence Company): GCAT launches of the last 30 days, from its published snapshot; and its frozen launch ledger file (orbit releases/ledger), read once to begin Launch's own LL2 ledger. Scheduled launches come from Launch's own schedule lane, and NGA warnings from Cordon
sources.licence: Each item keeps its source's terms: GCAT CC BY 4.0; Launch Library 2 free access, no licence stated; NGA US Government work; Japan Coast Guard Government Standard Terms of Use 2.0

sources.name: Launch Library 2, The Space Devs: upcoming launches (the schedule lane) and every launch since 1 Jan 2024 (the LL2 ledger), read directly from 19 Nov 2026 (Ascent move, from Orbit)
sources.licence: Free access to the whole database ("the entire database is accessible to everyone, for free", thespacedevs.com/llapi, read 16 Nov 2026), 15 requests an hour without a key. No separate data licence is stated; decided 15 Nov 2026: freely available, so it is used and republished with credit (Orbit's ledger release, now Launch's). Images not used: each carries its own licence.
sources.note: Two or three requests a Launch run (one upcoming, one ledger pull, at most one by-id lookup). While Orbit's lanes still run (1-2 an hour plus 4 a day), the two programs together stay well under 15 an hour.

sources.name: Spaceflight News API (Spaceflight News API and The Space Devs): headlines tied to Launch Library 2 launches, links only
sources.licence: No licence, terms of use or rate limit stated (site read 15 Nov 2026; footer 'Copyright 2026 Spaceflight News API & The Space Devs'). Links only: headline, outlet, time and the link to the outlet's page; no summaries, no images.
sources.note: One request a run, filtered to the scheduled launches' Launch Library 2 ids (Orbit's rule, orbit-2.5, decided 15 Nov 2026: links only). The API usually links the right launch (B); the headlines are the outlets' own reporting, not checked (3).

sources.licence: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026-PRESENT Joey0609 (repository LICENSE, read 16 Nov 2026; a copy is published beside the data as data/JOEY-NOTAMS-LICENSE.txt). vetting.question: Is the repository's live update timely enough for a live lane? Launch reads it at a pinned commit, for history only.
vetting.lead_time: 19 of 19 Chinese orbital launches, 13 Sep - 12 Nov 2026 (GCAT), had a notice of 6 h or less holding the launch within 1 h and within 2,800 km of the pad. Earliest notice's CREATED time before launch: median 142 h, range 97.5-252 h.
vetting.pickup: 13 launch-related notices created since 16 Nov 2026 reached the repository within 0.1-0.3 h of CREATED. Commit gaps over the last 14 days: median 1.6 h, longest 74.5 h. Earlier history was loaded in bulk, so it cannot show pickup.
vetting.sample: A6096/26 (ZLHW), created 03:03Z 20 Nov, window 21:06-21:36Z 29 Nov 2026: no Chinese Launch Library 2 record in that window at Launch's 01:15Z 21 Nov read. A closure, not a confirmed launch.

vetting.terms: API page read. /terms answers 404; no terms of use found.

vetting.sample: Next 5 read 21 Nov 2026: a CASC launch from Taiyuan at 03:50Z 21 Nov (record modified 18 Nov) was not among the 16 Launch Library 2 records Launch published from its 01:15Z read. USSF-266 is 23 Nov here and 24 Nov in Launch Library 2.
